title: should have an accessible socket id equal to the server-side socket id (default namespace)
review_note: Assertion audit: Initially recovered is false; receive ordinary events to establish offset; forcibly close the real transport; reconnect preserves namespace SID and sets recovered true (both property and connect payload). Native server-side transport kill replaces direct JS engine.close, and missed-event replay is additionally verified.

title: should connect to localhost
review_note: Assertion audit: Original pre-connect hi request is buffered, a real localhost server emits hi, the handler runs and the socket disconnects.

title: should not connect when autoConnect option set to false
review_note: Assertion audit: Explicit autoConnect false leaves the engine absent before disconnect; native active flag also remains false.

title: should start two connections with same path
review_note: JS io() URL inference/global manager cache is not Swift explicit SocketManager/namespace construction.

title: should start two connections with same path and different querystrings
review_note: JS io() URL inference/global manager cache is not Swift explicit SocketManager/namespace construction.

title: should start two connections with different paths
review_note: JS io() URL inference/global manager cache is not Swift explicit SocketManager/namespace construction.

title: should start a single connection with different namespaces
review_note: Assertion audit: /foo and /bar reference the identical manager, then both disconnect. Native explicit manager construction replaces JS io() lookup; global lookup behavior remains an API boundary.

title: should work with acks
review_note: Assertion audit: Emit the request before connection; server sends an event with an acknowledgement callback; client sends both original arguments 5 and {test:true}; server validates both and confirms via an event. Only fixture event names are renamed.

title: should receive date with ack
review_note: Assertion audit: Original pre-connect getAckDate with {test:true} receives a string acknowledgement from the real server; the native legacy NO ACK timeout sentinel is explicitly rejected.

title: should work with false
review_note: Assertion audit: Original pre-connect false request receives a server event containing Bool false, neither nil nor a truthy replacement.

title: should receive utf8 multibyte characters
review_note: Assertion audit: Request before connection, receive the five exact upstream UTF8 strings as server events including the repeated final string, assert count and full ordered equality. Only fixture event names are renamed.

title: should connect to a namespace after connection established
review_note: Assertion audit: Root connects first; /foo is created and joined inside its connect callback; /foo connects while root stays connected, then both close.

title: should open a new namespace after connection gets closed
review_note: Assertion audit: Root disconnects in its first connect callback; /foo is created and joined inside root disconnect; /foo successfully connects and disconnects.

title: should reconnect by default
review_note: Assertion audit: Default reconnect is not overridden: a real established server transport is dropped; the socket observes disconnect, successful reconnect and namespace connect in that order, with a working server ACK afterward. Native explicit connect replaces JS autoConnect; server-side transport termination replaces engine.close and a connect barrier replaces the fixed 100 ms delay.

title: should reconnect manually
review_note: Assertion audit: Initial connect disconnects; the one-shot disconnect callback reconnects synchronously; the second connect succeeds and disconnects. Exactly two connects.

title: should reconnect automatically after reconnecting manually
review_note: Assertion audit: Initial connect triggers disconnect; its callback calls connect reentrantly. After that manual connection a real transport drop must produce reconnect(attempt 1) before the namespace rejoins. Three total connects are asserted. Native socket lifecycle events expose manager events; a real handshake barrier replaces the JS 100 ms delay before engine termination.

title: should attempt reconnects after a failed reconnect
review_note: Assertion audit: Real connectTimeout(0), two retries and reconnectFailed; connect is invoked inside the first reconnectFailed callback, then the second cycle must fail with a fresh two-attempt budget (four total attempts, two failures). Native one-second backoff replaces JS 10 ms and manager events are observed on the socket.

title: reconnect delay should increase every time
review_note: Assertion audit: Real timeout(0), three retries, jitter 0.2: measure monotonic elapsed time from each opening error to reconnectAttempt, assert exactly [1,2,3], strictly increasing three actual intervals, then reconnectFailed. Native whole-second backoff scales the original 100 ms intervals by ten; the default cap does not truncate the third interval. Manager error is observed through native connectError.

title: should not reconnect when force closed
review_note: Assertion audit: Real opening timeout must occur, disconnect inside its error callback, then no reconnectAttempt over a window longer than the initial jittered retry delay. Native connectError exposes the opening error; seconds replace JS millisecond timing and the namespace is irrelevant because timeout precedes joining.

title: should stop reconnecting when force closed
review_note: Assertion audit: Real timeout(0); disconnect in first reconnectAttempt, observe long enough for another retry, assert exactly one attempt. Native seconds scale the observation window and socket events expose manager events.

title: should reconnect after stopping reconnection
review_note: Assertion audit: Real timeout(0); disconnect and connect in the same first reconnectAttempt callback; await and assert a subsequent attempt. Native socket event API and seconds replace manager emitter and millisecond backoff; teardown closes the retrying socket.

title: should stop reconnecting on a socket and keep to reconnect on another
review_note: Assertion audit: Shared manager with root and /asd first connected; terminate real transport, disconnect root inside reconnectAttempt, await /asd rejoining, then assert root still has exactly one connect while /asd has reconnected. Native socket lifecycle events expose manager events; handshake barriers and a server-side transport kill replace timed engine.close.

title: should try to reconnect twice and fail when requested two attempts with immediate timeout and reconnect enabled
review_note: Assertion audit: Real timeout(0), reconnectAttempts(2), await reconnectFailed and assert attempts exactly [1,2]. Native socket exposes manager lifecycle events; one-second backoff replaces JS 10 ms; namespace name cannot affect an opening timeout.

title: should fire reconnect_* events on manager
review_note: Assertion audit: Original executable assertions: timeout(0), reconnectAttempts(2), reconnectAttempt carries sequential numbers 1 then 2, and reconnectFailed ends the cycle with exactly two attempts. All are checked together against real timers. Native socket lifecycle subscription replaces the JS manager event emitter, not an exclusion.

title: should fire reconnecting (on manager) with attempts number when reconnecting twice
review_note: Assertion audit: Original repeats the timeout(0), two attempts, sequential 1-based reconnectAttempt payload and reconnectFailed scenario. The native test asserts the exact [1,2] sequence at failure with real opening timers; socket subscriptions expose manager events.

title: should not try to reconnect and should form a connection when connecting to correct port with default timeout
review_note: Assertion audit: Connect real /valid with reconnect enabled and default opening timeout, then observe beyond the first retry interval: connected status and zero reconnectAttempt callbacks. Native seconds scale the original observation period.

title: should connect while disconnecting another socket
review_note: Assertion audit: Real /foo connect callback starts /asd and disconnects /foo in that same callback; await /asd connect and assert it is connected while /foo is disconnected. Native explicit connect replaces implicit JS manager autoConnect.

title: should emit a connect_error event when reaching a Socket.IO server in v2.x
review_note: Assertion audit: Inject original root CONNECT with no sid/payload into the socket; exactly the incompatible-server connect_error is observed, connect does not fire and status does not become connected. Old protocol rejection remains supported; no old protocol implementation is required.

title: should not close the connection when disconnecting a single socket
review_note: Assertion audit: Real /foo and /asd namespaces share a manager. Closing /foo does not disconnect /asd; closing the last namespace then disconnects the manager and closes its engine. A native engine-close observer and closed-state assertion replace the JS manager close event bus.

title: should stop trying to reconnect
review_note: Assertion audit: Real refused port produces reconnectError after the first attempt; disable reconnects in that error callback (not reconnectAttempt), then assert that callback ran and only one attempt occurred over the observation window. Native socket emitter carries manager events and seconds replace JS millisecond timing.

title: should try to reconnect twice and fail when requested two attempts with incorrect address and reconnect enabled
review_note: Assertion audit: Real refused localhost port with retries enabled and budget two: await reconnectFailed and assert exactly two attempts. The concrete unused port and namespace spelling differ; connection refusal occurs before namespace join. Native socket receives manager events.

title: should not try to reconnect with incorrect port when reconnection disabled
review_note: Assertion audit: Real refused localhost port with reconnects false must emit connectError and report terminal failure, then zero retry attempts throughout an observation window longer than the configured retry interval. Native terminal error/disconnect representations are accepted only with a non-nil reason.

title: should still try to reconnect twice after opening another socket asynchronously
review_note: Assertion audit: Real refused port and two-attempt budget: asynchronously open another namespace during the initial backoff; await reconnectFailed and assert second namespace was opened and exactly two attempts occurred. Native explicit connect replaces JS manager autoConnect; delay is scaled within the initial native backoff.

title: should use native setTimeout with useNativeSetTimers

title: should emit date in object
review_note: Assertion audit: Original getDateObj request is emitted before connect; takeDateObj server event is a dictionary whose date field is a String.

title: should get base64 data as a last resort
review_note: Assertion audit: Request original getbin before connect on forced-base64 polling; assert b64=1 transport negotiation and received bytes re-encode exactly as YXNkZmFzZGY=. Native Data replaces the legacy JS {base64:true,data:...} wrapper used when ArrayBuffer/Blob are unavailable. The transferable binary content and base64 transport are tested; Swift does not emulate absence of native binary storage.

title: should get binary data (as an ArrayBuffer)
review_note: Assertion audit: Start connect and emit doge before joining; actual server returns binary bytes for asdfasdf. Assert Data type and exact bytes, separately on polling and WebSocket. Foundation.Data is the native binary representation replacing ArrayBuffer.

title: should send binary data (as an ArrayBuffer)
review_note: Assertion audit: Emit buffa while connecting with the exact bytes decoded from original base64 asdfasdf. Await buffack, emitted only if the real server received a Buffer; run on polling and WebSocket. Data replaces ArrayBuffer, with identical bytes.

title: should send binary data (as an ArrayBuffer) mixed with json
review_note: Assertion audit: Emit jsonbuff before connect with hello=lol, goodbye=gotcha and the original permissively decoded howdy bytes [134,140,29]. Real server checks both strings and Buffer type before emitting jsonbuff-ack. Run polling and WebSocket; native Data replaces ArrayBuffer.

title: should send events with ArrayBuffers in the correct order
review_note: Assertion audit: Start connect and emit original abuff1 binary [105,187,159,127], then abuff2 with please arrive second. Real server only emits abuff2-ack when abuff1 arrived first as binary. Native Data replaces ArrayBuffer; no artificial connection barrier.

title: should reopen a cached socket
review_note: Assertion audit: AutoConnect enabled: first connect disconnects; inside that disconnect callback fetch the same namespace, assert object identity and active true immediately, then await its second connect. Native manager.defaultSocket uses the same namespace cache as socket(forNamespace:).

title: should not reopen a cached but active socket
review_note: Assertion audit: AutoConnect manager: fetch same active root namespace twice before handshake completion and assert identity. On connect, disconnect and assert exact packet-create sequence [0,1] through a recording subclass of the real SocketEngine. Only explicit native root namespace spelling is canonicalized: 0/, to 0 and 1/, to 1.

title: should not reopen an already active socket
review_note: Assertion audit: AutoConnect manager opens root and /foo, then disconnects both from root connect callback. Assert exact real engine packet-create sequence [0,0/foo,,1,1/foo,], including no duplicate CONNECTs and subscription order. Native explicit root CONNECT/DISCONNECT namespace syntax alone is canonicalized.

title: should close the engine upon decoding exception
review_note: Assertion audit: Inject bad data through the manager engine-data entry point on a real connection. Assert parse-error disconnect, reconnect signal before reconnection, new engine object, retired engine closed, and different namespace SID. Listener setup uses the native namespace connect callback; the original engine identity and closed-state assertions are explicit.

title: should preserve the order of the packets
review_note: Assertion audit: Original retry budget one and emits echo 1,2,3 before connect: immediate queue lengths 1,2,3; ACK-time lengths 2,1,0; final nil error and integer 3; complete ordered ACK values. Real engine packet-create recorder additionally asserts CONNECT, ACK IDs 0/1/2 with exact echo payloads, then DISCONNECT. Native positive deadline scaled to two seconds; only explicit root CONNECT/DISCONNECT namespace is canonicalized.

title: should fail when the server does not acknowledge the packet
review_note: Ported 2026-09-19 (round 3): a retried head whose budget is spent is discarded with the close error, JS `packet.tryCount > this._opts.retries` inside `_clearAcks`. See ProtocolParityReview.md section 9.1.

title: should not drain the queue while the socket is disconnected
review_note: Ported 2026-09-19 (round 3): the queue does not drain while disconnected and the head keeps its place across a drop that reconnects. See ProtocolParityReview.md section 9.1.

title: should not emit a packet twice in the 'connect' handler
review_note: Ported 2026-09-19 (round 3): `onconnect` force-drains the retained head under a fresh ack id before the connect event, so it is not sent twice. See ProtocolParityReview.md section 9.1.

title: should have an accessible socket id equal to the server-side socket id (default namespace)
review_note: Assertion audit: Default namespace SID is nonempty, equals the independently queried server SID and differs from the Engine.IO SID. The connected socket then disconnects.

title: should have an accessible socket id equal to the server-side socket id (custom namespace)
review_note: Assertion audit: Custom /foo namespace SID is nonempty, equals the independently queried server SID and differs from Engine.IO SID; root and /foo SIDs are distinct.

title: clears socket.id upon disconnection
review_note: Assertion audit: SID is already empty inside the disconnect callback after explicitly disconnecting a connected socket, not merely after waiting for the callback.

title: doesn't fire an error event if we force disconnect in opening state
review_note: Assertion audit: Begin real connect with timeout 100 ms, immediately disconnect, and observe 1.5 seconds (longer than original 300 ms). Assert neither error nor connectError occurred; native socket error events expose manager opening errors.

title: fire a connect_error event when the connection cannot be established
review_note: Assertion audit: Connect real refused localhost:9823 with 100 ms opening timeout, require connectError, then disconnect in that callback. Native explicit connect replaces autoConnect.

title: fire a connect_error event on open timeout (polling)
review_note: Assertion audit: Real polling-only transport with opening timeout zero must emit connectError with exact timeout message. Native String error payload replaces JS Error.message; reconnect is disabled to isolate the first failure.

title: fire a connect_error event on open timeout (websocket)
review_note: Assertion audit: Real WebSocket-only transport with opening timeout zero must emit connectError with exact timeout message. Native String error payload replaces JS Error.message; reconnect is disabled to isolate the first failure.

title: doesn't fire a connect_error event when the connection is already established
review_note: Assertion audit: Real established transport drop: collect connectError events and require none through disconnect, successful reconnect and a following server ACK barrier. Also assert exact lifecycle order. Server-side transport termination replaces JS engine.close; native runtime error diagnostics are separate from connectError.

title: should change socket.id upon reconnection
review_note: Assertion audit: Real established socket ID captured, transport terminated, require reconnectAttempt observing cleared ID, reconnect observing an ID different from the old value, and subsequent namespace connect with a fresh ID. Require that attempt and reconnect callbacks actually ran. Native socket lifecycle emitter exposes manager events.

title: should enable compression by default
review_note: Excluded: native URLSession exposes no JS compression enable/disable or threshold controls; deflate interoperability remains tested.

title: should disable compression
review_note: Excluded: native URLSession exposes no JS compression enable/disable or threshold controls; deflate interoperability remains tested.

title: should accept an object (default namespace)
review_note: Assertion audit: Configure query object e=f, start real connect and immediately request getHandshake by ACK before connect completes; assert handshake.query.e is f. Native connectParams and legacy ACK callback replace JS query and emit callback.

title: should accept a query string (default namespace)
review_note: Assertion audit: URL query c=d on root, start real connect and immediately request getHandshake by ACK; assert handshake.query.c equals d. No pre-emit connect barrier.

title: should accept an object
review_note: Assertion audit: Real /abc namespace with connectParams a=b receives unsolicited handshake event and asserts query.a is b. Native explicit namespace selection replaces JS namespace in URL.

title: should accept a query string
review_note: Assertion audit: Real /abc namespace with URL query b=c&d=e receives handshake and asserts both exact query values. Namespace is selected explicitly, URL retains the query.

title: should properly encode the parameters
review_note: Assertion audit: Real /abc handshake receives exact query key &a and value &=?a without URL delimiter corruption; asserts decoded value equals original. Native connectParams replaces JS query object.

title: should accept an object
review_note: Assertion audit: Fresh manager and /abc namespace with original auth object {a:b,c:d}; server handshake echoes exact auth and both keys are absent from query. Explicit native connect replaces JS auto-connect.

title: should accept an function
review_note: Assertion audit: Fresh manager and /abc namespace with callback auth provider returning original {e:f}; server handshake echoes exact auth and e is absent from query. Explicit native connect replaces JS auto-connect.

title: should fire an error event on middleware failure from custom namespace
review_note: Assertion audit: Real /no namespace middleware refuses connection; connect_error contains the exact original Auth failed (custom namespace) message. Native payload representation replaces the JS Error instance.

title: should fire a connect_error event with error data on middleware failure
review_note: Assertion audit: Real /with-data rejection includes the exact original message and data object with exactly code=401 and details=Invalid token. Native dictionary replaces JS Error.data representation.

title: should not try to reconnect after a middleware failure
review_note: Assertion audit: After /no middleware rejection force an Engine.IO reconnect; a sibling root reconnect and server processing barrier prove the new connection is active. Refused namespace reports exactly one connect_error and sends no additional CONNECT; explicit frame count is three.

title: should properly disconnect then reconnect
review_note: Assertion audit: WebSocket-only first connect calls disconnect then connect in the same handler; reconnection succeeds and exactly one disconnect occurs before final cleanup.

title: should throw on reserved event
review_note: Assertion audit: On namespace /no, emit original reserved disconnecting event with goodbye; assert exactly one synchronous error containing the exact quoted name and reserved-event message, plus no buffered packet. Native nonthrowing emit reports through error event rather than a JS throw; rejection and diagnostic are preserved.

title: should emit events in order
review_note: Follow-up 2026-09-19: assertion-port. A pre-connect buffered emit is acknowledged before an emit from the connect callback; real server, explicit polling and WebSocket cases plus upgrade enabled. See JavaScriptParityContracts.json for exact executable evidence.

title: should emit an event and wait for the acknowledgement
review_note: Assertion audit: Start connection then immediately await echo(123); real server acknowledgement resolves the async result with 123. Explicit connect replaces JS auto-connect, with no wait-for-connect barrier.

title: should discard a volatile packet when the socket is not connected
review_note: Assertion audit: Original volatile getId request before connection never receives its callback; the following reliable request is buffered and acknowledged by a real server after connect. Native fixture event is server-socket-id; dropped untimed acknowledgement is additionally not retained.

title: should discard a volatile packet when the pipe is not ready
review_note: Assertion audit: Controlled engine writability covers connected busy pipe and disconnected pipe: volatile getId never sends or acknowledges, while reliable getId reaches the engine and its server-id acknowledgement completes. Explicit writability replaces the timing-dependent JS first-write backpressure setup; no buffer/ack registration for the dropped packet.

title: should send a volatile packet when the socket is connected and the pipe is ready
review_note: Assertion audit: Repeat volatile server-ID request every 200ms across connection establishment until the real transport accepts it and the server acknowledgement succeeds; stop interval and check no retry-queue entry. Native fixture event is server-socket-id.

title: should call listener
review_note: Assertion audit: Real /abc handshake reaches incoming catch-all with event name handshake and an object argument; lifecycle events do not pollute this observation.

title: should prepend listener
review_note: Assertion audit: Original ordinary listener followed by two prepended listeners on /abc; server handshake invokes them in exact LIFO-prepend order 0,1,2.

title: should remove listener
review_note: Assertion audit: Register then remove the sole catch-all by its native UUID; count is zero, removed callback must never fire, and a replacement receives the real /abc handshake.

title: should call listener
review_note: Assertion audit: After real /abc connection, emit original my-event with String 123; outgoing catch-all receives the exact name and argument. Also repeated for an emit buffered before connection.

title: should call listener with binary data
review_note: Follow-up 2026-09-19: assertion-port. Inside connect, install an outgoing listener and immediately emit binary without an intervening queue turn; assert event name, original bytes, one call and server echo. See JavaScriptParityContracts.json for exact executable evidence.

title: should prepend listener
review_note: Assertion audit: Ordinary outgoing listener plus two prepended listeners observe original pre-connect my-event(123) in exact 0,1,2 order only after connection; also checked for an emit inside connect callback.

title: should remove listener
review_note: Follow-up 2026-09-19: native-assertion-equivalent. Removing a UUID listener is effective before the immediately following emit on the owning queue; removed callback must not fire and listener count is zero. See JavaScriptParityContracts.json for exact executable evidence.

title: should timeout after the given delay when socket is not connected
review_note: Assertion audit: Disconnected emit of event with a 50 ms timeout: assert timeout error and zero buffered packets inside the timeout callback, then simulate CONNECT and assert no expired packet is sent. Native testRetainedBuffers exposes the original private sendBuffer assertion; this local timer scenario needs no server.

title: should timeout when the server does not acknowledge the event
review_note: Assertion audit: Start connection to the real server and immediately emit unknown with a 50 ms explicit timeout, without a connect barrier; callback must report SocketAckError.timeout. Native explicit connect replaces JS autoConnect.

title: should timeout when the server does not acknowledge the event in time
review_note: Assertion audit: Start real connection, immediately emit echo 42 with zero timeout, assert timeout error and exactly one callback after 200 ms. Additionally repeat on an established connection, wait for a subsequent server ACK as an ordered wire barrier behind the expired echo ACK, and assert exactly one callback and no pending ACK. Count every callback regardless of outcome, so a second successful ACK cannot evade the negative assertion.

title: should not timeout when the server does acknowledge the event
review_note: Assertion audit: Real server: start connect and emit echo 42 immediately, without awaiting connect; explicit timed callback must receive nil error and integer 42. Native timeout scaled to five seconds for CI, preserving before-deadline semantics; default-timeout emit and ping/pong are not used as substitutes.

title: should timeout when the server does not acknowledge the event (promise)
review_note: Assertion audit: Real server: start connect and immediately await timeout(50 ms).emitWithAck(unknown); resolution fails the test, rejection must be SocketAckError.timeout. Swift async/throws replaces JS promise rejection.

title: should not timeout when the server does acknowledge the event (promise)
review_note: Assertion audit: Start connection then await timed echo(42); real server acknowledgement returns 42 without throwing. Timeout uses native seconds and a CI-safe five-second success budget instead of JS 50ms; no wait-for-connect barrier.

title: should use the default timeout value
review_note: Assertion audit: Configure ackTimeout 50 ms, start real connect and immediately emit unknown with a plain callback and no explicit timeout; assert SocketAckError.timeout. Native manager default is inherited by the socket; explicit connect replaces autoConnect.

title: should not ack upon disconnection (callback)
review_note: Assertion audit: Connect to real server, emit echo a with modern untimed ACK callback and immediately enqueue disconnect on the same handle queue. Assert empty pending ACK registry and inverted expectation proving callback never fires after disconnect, including delayed server responses. Native error-first callback is the supported plain ACK surface; legacy sentinel API is not used as evidence.

title: should ack with an error upon disconnection (callback & timeout)
review_note: Ported 2026-09-19 (round 3): `socket.timeout(N).emit` settles with the disconnect error and leaves an empty registry, asserted on a transport drop that reconnects, not only on `disconnect()`. See ProtocolParityReview.md section 9.1.

title: should ack with an error upon disconnection (callback & ackTimeout)
review_note: Ported 2026-09-19 (round 3): the configured-`ackTimeout` callback settles on a retried drop too, including the real server-side transport kill; a callback registered without `withError` is removed silently. See ProtocolParityReview.md section 9.1.

title: should ack with an error upon disconnection (promise)
review_note: Ported 2026-09-19 (round 3): the `emitWithAck` continuation is resumed with `.disconnected` on a drop that reconnects, as JS rejects the promise from `_clearAcks`. See ProtocolParityReview.md section 9.1.

title: should ack with an error upon disconnection (promise & timeout)
review_note: Assertion audit: Real established connection: await timeout(10 s).emitWithAck(echo,a); outgoing listener queues disconnect immediately after send registration, before a server ACK can return. Assert actual send, rejection with SocketAckError.disconnected within five seconds (before timeout), and empty ACK registry. This replaces synthetic didDisconnect-only evidence with the public disconnect API.

title: should not discard an unsent ack (callback)
review_note: Ported 2026-09-19 (round 3): an ack whose packet is still in the send buffer survives the close and is answered after the reconnect, JS `sendBuffer.some(...)` inside `_clearAcks`. See ProtocolParityReview.md section 9.1.

title: should buffer the event and send it upon reconnection
review_note: Ported 2026-09-19 (round 3): an expired ping deadline buffers the emit, and its acknowledgement survives the close and is answered once the buffer is flushed on the next CONNECT. See ProtocolParityReview.md section 9.1.
